title: Zi package manifest, version 1
description: Shape of package.json for a Zi package. Zi reads only the zsh-data object; every other member is metadata for humans and registries. Rules that span zsh-data members, such as an is-snippet profile requiring plugin-info.url, are not expressible here and are enforced by scripts/validate-package-manifest.py.

version.description: Registry metadata only. Zi never reads it. Prefer omitting it: where it exists today it duplicates an upstream version that nothing updates.

schema.description: Version of this contract the manifest targets.

pluginInfo.description: The five fields Zi reads are user, plugin, url, message and requires. Which identity fields apply depends on the source mode each profile declares.

user.description: GitHub owner. Used when a profile declares git or from.

plugin.description: GitHub repository name. Used when a profile declares git or from.

url.description: Direct download URL, used when a profile declares is-snippet. Evaluated by the shell, so it may contain Zsh parameter expansion such as ${(M)OSTYPE#(linux|darwin)}. It is not an inert string.

message.description: Shown to the user before the package installs.

requires.description: Semicolon-separated tokens. bgn, dl and rdl name annex capabilities; any other token names a command that must be present.

ziIces.description: One entry per installation profile. `default` is what `zi pack` selects when no profile is named, so it is mandatory. Other names are free-form.

profile.description: An ice-list. Values are shell strings, so JSON numbers and booleans are not permitted even where they would parse. Exactly one source mode must be declared: is-snippet selects plugin-info.url, git or from selects plugin-info.user and plugin. Declaring none falls through to an npm _from tarball path that no manifest populates, which downloads an empty URL.
